Varying effects

  • Varying intercepts
  • Varying intercepts and slopes
  • Nested varying effects
  • Python
  • R
  • Julia
from BayesForge import bf
import numpy as np

# Setup device------------------------------------------------
m = bf(platform='cpu')

# Import Data & Data Manipulation ------------------------------------------------
# Import
data_path = m.load.reedfrogs(only_path=True)
m.data(data_path, sep=';')
# Manipulate
m.df["tank"] = np.arange(m.df.shape[0])
N_tanks = m.df.shape[0]

# Define model ------------------------------------------------
def model(tank, surv, density):
    alpha = m.effects.varying_intercept(N_groups=N_tanks, group_id=tank, group_name='tank')
    m.dist.binomial(total_count=density, logits=alpha, obs=surv)

# Run sampler ------------------------------------------------
m.fit(model)

# Diagnostic ------------------------------------------------
m.summary()
library(BayesForge)

# Setup device------------------------------------------------
m <- importBF(platform = "cpu")

# Import Data & Data Manipulation ------------------------------------------------
# Import
data_path <- m$load$reedfrogs(only_path = TRUE)
m$data(data_path, sep = ";")
# Manipulate
m$df$tank <- 0:(nrow(m$df) - 1)
N_tanks <- nrow(m$df)
jnp <- reticulate::import("jax.numpy")
m$data_on_model <- list(
  tank    = jnp$array(as.integer(m$df$tank)),
  surv    = jnp$array(as.integer(m$df$surv)),
  density = jnp$array(as.integer(m$df$density))
)

# Define model ------------------------------------------------
model <- function(tank, surv, density) {
  alpha <- m$effects$varying_intercept(N_groups = N_tanks, group_id = tank, group_name = "tank")
  m$dist$binomial(total_count = density, logits = alpha, obs = surv)
}

# Run sampler ------------------------------------------------
m$fit(model)

# Diagnostic ------------------------------------------------
m$summary()

from BayesForge import bf
import jax.numpy as jnp
from importlib.resources import files

# Setup device------------------------------------------------
m = bf(platform='cpu')

# Import Data & Data Manipulation ------------------------------------------------
data_path = files('BayesForge.Resources') / 'Sim data multivariatenormal.csv'
m.data(data_path, sep=',')
m.data_on_model = dict(
    cafe=jnp.array(m.df.cafe.values, dtype=jnp.int32),
    wait=jnp.array(m.df.wait.values, dtype=jnp.float32),
    N_cafes=len(m.df.cafe.unique()),
    afternoon=jnp.array(m.df.afternoon.values, dtype=jnp.float32),
)

# Define model ------------------------------------------------
def model(cafe, wait, N_cafes, afternoon):
    a = m.dist.normal(5, 2, shape=(1,), name='a')
    b = m.dist.normal(-1, 0.5, shape=(1,), name='b')
    sigma = m.dist.exponential(1, name='sigma')

    varying_intercept, varying_slope = m.effects.varying_effects(
        N_vars=1,              # one slope (afternoon)
        N_group=N_cafes,
        group_id=cafe,
        group_name='cafe',
        alpha_bar=a,           # global intercept
        beta_bar=b)            # global slope

    mu = varying_intercept + varying_slope * afternoon
    m.dist.normal(mu, sigma, obs=wait)

# Run sampler ------------------------------------------------
m.fit(model)
library(BayesForge)
jnp <- reticulate::import("jax.numpy")
resources <- reticulate::import("importlib.resources")

# Setup device------------------------------------------------
m <- importBF(platform = "cpu")

# Import Data & Data Manipulation ------------------------------------------------
data_path <- resources$files("BayesForge.Resources")$joinpath("Sim data multivariatenormal.csv")
m$data(data_path, sep = ",")
m$data_on_model <- list(
  cafe = jnp$array(as.integer(m$df$cafe), dtype = jnp$int32),
  wait = jnp$array(as.numeric(m$df$wait), dtype = jnp$float32),
  N_cafes = length(unique(m$df$cafe)),
  afternoon = jnp$array(as.numeric(m$df$afternoon), dtype = jnp$float32)
)

# Define model ------------------------------------------------
model <- function(cafe, wait, N_cafes, afternoon) {
  a <- m$dist$normal(5, 2, shape = reticulate::tuple(1L), name = "a")
  b <- m$dist$normal(-1, 0.5, shape = reticulate::tuple(1L), name = "b")
  sigma <- m$dist$exponential(1, name = "sigma")

  effects <- m$effects$varying_effects(
    N_vars = 1L,             # one slope (afternoon)
    N_group = N_cafes,
    group_id = cafe,
    group_name = "cafe",
    alpha_bar = a,           # global intercept
    beta_bar = b)            # global slope
  varying_intercept <- effects[[1]]
  varying_slope <- effects[[2]]

  mu <- varying_intercept + varying_slope * afternoon
  m$dist$normal(mu, sigma, obs = wait)
}

# Run sampler ------------------------------------------------
m$fit(model)

end

from BayesForge import bf

# Setup device------------------------------------------------
m = bf(platform='cpu')

# Import Data & Data Manipulation ------------------------------------------------
# group_id / region_id are one obs-level index array per level (top to bottom).
# The parent structure (which region each group belongs to) is derived automatically.
data_path = m.load.sim_nested_effects(only_path=True)
m.data(data_path)

# Define model ------------------------------------------------
# N_vars = intercept + slopes; it is independent of the number of levels.
def model(y, x, group_id, region_id, N_groups=20, N_regions=5):
    sigma = m.dist.exponential(1)

    a_est, b_est = m.effects.nested_varying_effects(
        N_vars   = 2,                      # intercept + 1 slope
        names    = ["region", "group"],    # levels, top to bottom
        N_groups = [N_regions, N_groups],  # units at each level
        group_ids= [region_id, group_id],  # obs-level index per level
        centered = False,                  # non-centered (recommended)
    )

    mu = a_est + b_est * x
    m.dist.normal(mu, sigma, obs=y)

# Run sampler ------------------------------------------------
m.fit(model)
m.summary()
library(BayesForge)

# Setup device------------------------------------------------
m <- importBF(platform = "cpu")

# Import Data & Data Manipulation ------------------------------------------------
# group_id / region_id are one obs-level index array per level (top to bottom).
# The parent structure (which region each group belongs to) is derived automatically.
data_path <- m$load$sim_nested_effects(only_path = TRUE)
m$data(data_path)
jnp <- reticulate::import("jax.numpy")
m$data_on_model <- list(
  y         = jnp$array(m$df$y),
  x         = jnp$array(m$df$x),
  group_id  = jnp$array(as.integer(m$df$group_id)),
  region_id = jnp$array(as.integer(m$df$region_id))
)

# Define model ------------------------------------------------
# N_vars = intercept + slopes; it is independent of the number of levels.
model <- function(y, x, group_id, region_id, N_groups = 20L, N_regions = 5L) {
  sigma <- m$dist$exponential(1, name = "sigma")

  effects <- m$effects$nested_varying_effects(
    N_vars    = 2L,                            # intercept + 1 slope
    names     = list("region", "group"),       # levels, top to bottom
    N_groups  = list(N_regions, N_groups),     # units at each level
    group_ids = list(region_id, group_id),     # obs-level index per level
    centered  = FALSE                          # non-centered (recommended)
  )
  a_est <- effects[[1]]
  b_est <- effects[[2]]

  mu <- a_est + b_est * x
  m$dist$normal(mu, sigma, obs = y, name = "y")
}

# Run sampler ------------------------------------------------
m$fit(model)
m$summary()
using PyBayesForge
using PythonCall

# Setup device------------------------------------------------
m = importBF(platform="cpu")

# Import Data & Data Manipulation ------------------------------------------------
# group_id / region_id are one obs-level index array per level (top to bottom).
# The parent structure (which region each group belongs to) is derived automatically.
data_path = m.load.sim_nested_effects(only_path=true)
m.data(data_path)

# Define model ------------------------------------------------
# N_vars = intercept + slopes; it is independent of the number of levels.
@BF function model(y, x, group_id, region_id)
    N_groups = 20
    N_regions = 5
    sigma = m.dist.exponential(1, name="sigma")

    a_est, b_est = m.effects.nested_varying_effects(
        N_vars    = 2,                         # intercept + 1 slope
        names     = ["region", "group"],       # levels, top to bottom
        N_groups  = [N_regions, N_groups],     # units at each level
        group_ids = [region_id, group_id],     # obs-level index per level
        centered  = false,                     # non-centered (recommended)
    )

    mu = a_est + b_est * x
    m.dist.normal(mu, sigma, obs=y, name="y")
end

# Run sampler ------------------------------------------------
m.fit(model)
m.summary()

m.effects.nested_varying_effects generalizes to any depth (add levels to names, N_groups, group_ids) and any number of variables (N_vars = intercept + number of slopes, returned as a_est, b1, b2, ...). Pass centered=True for the centered parameterization, or supply per-level sigma / L_corr / corr priors to override the defaults. See Nested varying effects for the full model and math.

Network metrics

All metrics take an adjacency matrix (a JAX array) and can be used inside any model. See Network Metrics for definitions. The examples below use this small 4-node network:

  • Python
  • R
  • Julia
from BayesForge import bf
import jax.numpy as jnp
m = bf(platform='cpu')
adj_matrix_jax = jnp.array([[0, 1, 1, 0],
                            [1, 0, 1, 0],
                            [1, 1, 0, 1],
                            [0, 0, 1, 0]], dtype=jnp.float32)
library(BayesForge)
jnp <- reticulate::import("jax.numpy")
m <- importBF(platform = "cpu")
adj_matrix_jax <- jnp$array(rbind(c(0, 1, 1, 0),
                                  c(1, 0, 1, 0),
                                  c(1, 1, 0, 1),
                                  c(0, 0, 1, 0)), dtype = jnp$float32)
using PyBayesForge
using PythonCall
m = importBF(platform="cpu")
adj_matrix_jax = jnp.array([0 1 1 0;
                            1 0 1 0;
                            1 1 0 1;
                            0 0 1 0], dtype=jnp.float32)
